newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-STIANSEN FASTEST IN WORLD CUP SLALOM FIRST RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-STIANSEN FASTEST IN WORLD CUP SLALOM FIRST RUN.

text.p: Tom Stiansen of Norway stormed out of the number 22 start position to take the lead at the men's World Cup slalom in Breckenridge, Colorado, after the first run Sunday.

Taking advantage of a firm course that allowed late starters an equal opportunity, Stiansen posted a time of 51.75 seconds. Christian Mayer of Austria held second after the first run at 51.82 seconds, just ahead of Italy's Mario Reiter, clocked in 51.90.

Jure Kosir of Slovenia was fourth in 52.04 and Michael Von Gruenigen of Switzerland was fifth in 52.09. Thomas Sykora of Austria, winner of the season's first slalom a week earlier, had the sixth-fastest time, 52.13.
